Compile-Time Verification Payback & De Bruijn Caching [E/M · reported_j]

Pre-compiling librce_rt.rlib cuts cold rustc -O3 compile energy 20.07x on AMD Zen 5 and 15.44x on idle Intel Core i9; warm De Bruijn cache hits cut single-file rebuilds up to 448.5x.

1/2 Per-host Linux RAPL core/PP0 reported_j (20 kernels x 15 tiers):
- Cold prelude cut: 20.07x on Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (56.29->2.81 J) & 15.44x on idle Core i9-13900H (84.40->5.47 J)
- De Bruijn cache (de Bruijn 1972): 0/500 mutant collisions vs 150/150 naive ID-strip bugs

2/2 Candid boundaries:
- Refutes any universal descriptive compiler rule -> proposed 7-part contract
- Up to 448.5x (rustc -O3) & 167.8x (clang -O3) apply ONLY on warm renamed single-file hits (1.0x cold)
- -O2->-O3 never paid back on 20-30% of kernels; measured_j=null
